overall_reason: A marketing sentence pasted over four equal KPI tiles with no period, comparison, target or lead metric: the screen an agent produces for 'team dashboard' when nobody decided what the team needs to know.

findings.evidence: Four identical cards (same size, fill #f4f4f6, 20px radius, label + number) with no lead: T-FIVE-SECOND fails on 'what to do' and on 'what matters'; the eye has no first stop. Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: this is the stock 'KPI row' with nothing else.
findings.after: Promote the one metric the team acts on to a lead block with its trend and target; set the others as a compact secondary row [DATA NEEDED: which metric the team owns and its target]
findings.why: A dashboard with no lead metric is KPI confetti; ranking the numbers is the design decision that was skipped.

findings.evidence: T-SO-WHAT: '1,284', '4,017', '3.4%', '1.1%' have no period, no prior value, no direction and no target, so none can be judged good or bad; T-THREE-LINE: none is falsifiable as shown.
findings.after: Conversion 3.4% (last 30 days, up from 2.9%; target 4%) [DATA NEEDED: period, prior value, target]
findings.why: A single value needs a worded qualifier to mean anything.

findings.evidence: 'Powerful, intuitive, and beautiful reporting that lets your team unlock seamless insight across every workspace.' T-FRESH-READER: this line would fit any analytics product; it is landing-page copy inside an app screen and says nothing about the numbers below. Also a triplet of adjectives.
findings.before: "Powerful, intuitive, and beautiful reporting that lets your team unlock seamless insight across every workspace."
findings.after: State scope and freshness: 'All workspaces, last 30 days. Updated hourly.' [DATA NEEDED: real period and refresh]
findings.why: Marketing adjectives on a working screen are filler; the slot should orient the reader.

findings.evidence: The page ends after the KPI row; the remaining 660px is empty. There is no breakdown, list or action, so the dashboard cannot answer the follow-up question any number raises.
findings.after: Add the one view behind the lead metric (trend or list of what changed) [DATA NEEDED: series data]
findings.why: Density should match a data product; four bare numbers are not an overview.

strengths: Plain labels ('Active users', 'Sessions', 'Conversion', 'Churn') and tabular-looking numerals; tokens and dark-mode support carried from the shared base.
not_investigated: Whether the numbers are real: fixture data, no source supplied (sweep INT-007 already notes unsourced stat band).
